rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something is clearly noticeable or conspicuous, including a marked increase.

example.english: There is a marked crease on this sheet of paper.
example.traditional: 呢張紙有條明顯嘅摺痕。
example.jyutping: ni1 zoeng1 zi2 jau5 tiu4 ming4 hin2 ge3 zip3 han4

rows.note: Use this before a noun when it has a visible or identifying mark.

example.english: This is a marked box, so do not take the wrong one.
example.traditional: 呢個係有記號嘅箱，唔好拎錯。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hai6 jau5 gei3 hou6 ge3 soeng1 m4 hou2 ling1 co3

rows.note: Use this slice when marked means suspicious or regarded as suspect.

example.english: The police marked that man as suspicious.
example.traditional: 警察覺得嗰個男人可疑。
example.jyutping: ging2 caat3 gok3 dak1 go2 go3 naam4 jan4 ho2 ji4

rows.jyutping: bei2 jan4 ding1 soeng5 ge3 A
rows.note: Use this when a person has been singled out or targeted for hostility or revenge.

example.english: He is a marked man now, so he has to be careful outside.
example.traditional: 佢已經係俾人盯上嘅人，出街要小心。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ji5 ging1 hai6 bei2 jan4 deng1 soeng5 ge3 jan4 ceot1 gaai1 jiu3 siu2 sam1
